title: Bayesian Model Averaging for Self-Adaptive Multi-Agent Orchestration
research_question: Can Bayesian model averaging over competing workflow-performance models improve runtime task allocation and replanning in multi-agent AI systems compared with selecting a single orchestration model?
hypothesis: In multi-agent workflow optimization, maintaining and updating a weighted ensemble of competing orchestration models will reduce overconfident routing decisions and improve adaptation quality under changing task conditions, yielding more robust performance than single-model orchestration policies.
motivation: The knowledge base highlights an open gap in handling model-selection uncertainty inside self-adaptive systems: existing approaches often assume one best model, even though the cited work argues this can cause poor predictions and unnecessary or missed adaptations. That paper also explicitly flags future work on extending the approach to additional domains and heterogeneous requirements. A promising unexplored direction is to transfer this uncertainty-aware adaptation mechanism from robotic self-adaptive systems to AI agent orchestration, where workflow conditions, agent capabilities, and task decompositions shift over time. This aligns with the highest-priority tracked direction, agentic-workflow-optimization, and offers a concrete, falsifiable way to improve multi-agent robustness.
